question: Under section 8 of the Lake Basin Development Authority Act, what functions does the Authority have regarding planning and development of the Area?
ground_truth: Under section 8, the Authority's functions include planning for the development of the area and initiating project activities identified from such planning; developing an up-to-date long range development plan for the Area; initiating studies and surveys to assess demands on natural resources and to implement projects to exploit resources such as agriculture, forestry, wildlife, tourism, electric power generation, mining and fishing, and to recommend economic priorities; coordinating studies of schemes so that human, water, animal, land and other resources are utilized to best advantage and monitoring the design and execution of planned projects; monitoring and evaluating project performance to improve performance, establish responsibility, and improve future planning; coordinating the abstraction and use of natural resources, especially water, and setting up effective monitoring of such use; causing and effecting construction of works necessary for protection and utilization of water and soils; ensuring landowners undertake measures specified by the Authority to protect water and soils; and identifying, collecting, collating and correlating data related to the use of water.
title: Lake Basin Development Authority Act

question: Under the Insurance (Claims Management) Guidelines, 2022, within what timeframe must an insurance intermediary transmit a received claim notification to the insurer?
ground_truth: The intermediary must immediately transmit the claim notification to the insurer, and in any case not later than two (2) working days.
title: The Insurance (Claims Management) Guidelines, 2022

question: Under the Bank of Baroda (Kenya) Limited Act, what happens to existing contracts, deeds, leases, licences and other instruments entered into by Baroda once they vest in the New Bank?
ground_truth: As from the vesting day, all such existing contracts, agreements, conveyances, deeds, leases, licences, permits, exemptions, powers of attorney, undertakings, securities and other instruments made with or granted to Baroda, whose proper law is Kenyan law, become binding and of full force and effect against or in favour of the New Bank as if the New Bank had been a party to them instead of Baroda, and any reference to a Baroda director, officer or employee is treated as a reference to the corresponding director, officer or employee of the New Bank.
title: Bank of Baroda (Kenya) Limited Act

question: Under Article 32 of the International Interests in Aircraft Equipment Act (Protocol), what formal requirements must an assignment of associated rights meet for it to transfer the related international interest?
ground_truth: An assignment of associated rights transfers the related international interest only if it: (a) is in writing; (b) enables the associated rights to be identified under the contract from which they arise; and (c) in the case of an assignment by way of security, enables the obligations secured by the assignment to be determined in accordance with the Protocol but without the need to state a sum or maximum sum secured. Additionally, an assignment of an international interest created or provided for by a security agreement is not valid unless some or all related associated rights are also assigned, and the Convention does not apply to an assignment of associated rights that is not effective to transfer the related international interest.
title: International Interests in Aircraft Equipment Act

question: Under the Probation of Offenders Act, what can a court that made a probation order do if it is proved that the probationer was convicted of an offence committed while the probation order was in force?
ground_truth: If the probationer was not convicted of the original offence, the court may convict him of it and pass any sentence it could have passed had he just been convicted of that offence; if he was already convicted of the original offence, the court may pass any sentence it could pass had he just been convicted before it of that offence (section 7(4) of the Probation of Offenders Act).
title: Probation of Offenders Act

question: Under section 27 of the Tea Act, what penalty applies to a person convicted of illegally manufacturing, buying, selling or possessing tea grown or processed otherwise than in accordance with the Act?
ground_truth: On conviction, the person is liable to a fine not exceeding ten million shillings, or to imprisonment for a term not exceeding five years, or both.
title: Tea Act

question: Under the Price Control (Essential Goods) Act, what is the penalty for contravening the provisions of the Act, such as selling a commodity above the maximum price declared under section 2?
ground_truth: A person who contravenes the Act commits an offence and is liable on conviction to a fine not exceeding one million shillings, or to imprisonment for a term not exceeding five years, or to both.
title: Price Control (Essential Goods) Act

question: Under the Kenya Cultural Centre Act, what powers does the Council have with regard to appointing committees?
ground_truth: Under section 5A, the Council may from time to time appoint general or special committees of such number of persons as it thinks fit, to examine and report on any matter or perform any act more conveniently done by a committee. It may delegate to any such committee such powers as it thinks fit (except powers for which the Act makes special provision) and may fix the quorum of any committee. However, a committee's act is not binding on the Council until referred to and approved by the Council, unless the Council has by resolution authorized the committee to manage, regulate or conclude the matter. Each committee elects its own chairman (and may elect a deputy chairman) and, subject to the Act, regulates its own procedure.
title: Kenya Cultural Centre Act

question: Under section 13 of the Kenya Broadcasting Corporation Act, how is the full net cost of providing and transmitting external services to be funded?
ground_truth: The full net cost of providing and transmitting external services shall be borne from funds specially provided to the Corporation by Parliament for that purpose.
title: Kenya Broadcasting Corporation Act

question: Under the Kenya School of Law Act, how is the Director of the School appointed and what is their role in relation to the Board?
ground_truth: The Director is appointed by the Board through a competitive recruitment process on terms and conditions determined by the Board, and serves as the Chief Executive Officer of the School and Secretary to the Board. The Director is an ex officio member of the Board but has no right to vote, and is responsible, subject to the Board's direction, for the day-to-day management of the School's affairs.
title: Kenya School of Law Act

question: Under the Ferries Act, what procedure must the Road Authority follow before making an order prohibiting ferry services in a particular area under section 3(1)?
ground_truth: Before making the prohibition order, the Road Authority must publish notice of its intention in the Gazette and in at least one newspaper circulating in the district, once a week for four successive weeks; any objections received must be laid before the Cabinet Secretary, and only if the Cabinet Secretary approves after considering objections can the Road Authority make the order, which must then be published in the Gazette and a local newspaper and comes into force on the date specified in it.
title: Ferries Act

question: Under the Judicial Service Act, within what time frame must the Commission submit the annual report to the President and Parliament after the end of the financial year?
ground_truth: Section 38(1A) of the Judicial Service Act requires the Commission to submit the annual report to the President and Parliament within six months after the end of the year to which it relates.
title: Judicial Service Act

question: Under the Evidence Act, of what matters must a Kenyan court take judicial notice, such as the ordinary course of nature and the meaning of English words?
ground_truth: Under section 60 of the Evidence Act, a court must take judicial notice of matters including seals authorized by written law; accession to office, names, titles, functions and signatures of public officers notified in the Gazette; the existence, title and national flag of recognized States; natural and artificial divisions of time, geographical divisions of the world, and public holidays; the extent of Commonwealth territories; the commencement, continuance and termination of hostilities between Kenya and other States; the names of members and officers of the court and persons authorized to appear before it; the rule of the road on land, sea or air; the ordinary course of nature; the meaning of English words; matters of general or local notoriety; and any other matters it is directed by written law to notice.
title: Evidence Act

question: Under the Bukura Agricultural College Act, what powers does the Board have as the governing body of the College?
ground_truth: Under section 8 of the Bukura Agricultural College Act, the Board, as the governing body of the College, has power to: control, supervise and administer the College's assets to best promote its purpose; determine provisions for capital and recurrent expenditure and reserves; receive grants, gifts, donations or endowments and make legitimate disbursements from them; enter into association with other colleges, universities or institutions of higher learning; open banking accounts for the College's funds; invest surplus funds as provided in section 16; and, in consultation with the academic board, make regulations governing the conduct and discipline of students.
title: Bukura Agricultural College Act

question: Under the Auctioneers Act, is a licensed auctioneer required to obtain a separate licence to sell liquor, television, radio or video sets seized in execution of a court decree or in distress for rent?
ground_truth: No. Under section 14(6) of the Auctioneers Act, while a licence does not generally authorize dealing in or selling restricted items, the proviso specifically exempts an auctioneer from needing a separate licence to sell liquor, television, radio or video sets or other items seized in execution of a court decree or in distress for rent.
title: Auctioneers Act

question: Under the Trusts of Land Act, for how many years at most must an option to purchase or take a lease of trust land granted by trustees for sale be made exercisable?
ground_truth: Under section 22(2) of the Trusts of Land Act, every such option must be made exercisable within an agreed number of years not exceeding ten.
title: Trusts of Land Act

question: Under section 4 of the Trading in Prohibited Goods Act, can a legal owner of goods be held liable for an offence committed by their agent, clerk, or servant?
ground_truth: Yes. Where an act or omission by an agent, clerk or servant employed by the legal owner (or a person holding themselves out as the legal owner) would constitute an offence under the Act if done by the owner personally, the owner or person is liable for that offence as if they had done or omitted the act themselves, without prejudice to the liability of the agent, clerk or servant.
title: Trading in Prohibited Goods Act

question: Under the National Payment System Act, once settlement has been effected by an entry to the credit of a settlement system participant's account in the Central Bank settlement system or a designated payment system, can that settlement be reversed?
ground_truth: No. Under section 9(2) of the National Payment System Act, once settlement is effected by payment of money or by an entry to the credit of the account of a settlement system participant in the Central Bank settlement system or a designated payment system, that settlement is final and irrevocable.
title: National Payment System Act

question: Under section 6 of the Kenya Reinsurance Corporation Act, what happens to an existing account between the Kenya Reinsurance Corporation and a customer on the appointed day when the business is vested in the Company?
ground_truth: On and after the appointed day, the account becomes an account between the Company and the customer with the same rights and subject to the same obligations and incidents, including rights of set-off as before, and is deemed to be a single continuing account, though this does not affect any right of the Company or customer to vary the conditions or incidents of the account.
title: Kenya Reinsurance Corporation Act

question: Who was the presiding judge and what was the case number in Postal Corporation of Kenya v Straight Security Services Limited, a 2026 Court of Appeal ruling at Nairobi?
ground_truth: The case, Civil Application E696 of 2025, was heard at the Court of Appeal at Nairobi by Judge M Sila, with the ruling delivered on 25 March 2026.
title: Postal Corporation of Kenya v Straight Security Services Limited (Civil Application E696 of 2025) [2026] KECA 689 (KLR) (25 March 2026) (Ruling)

question: In Nzuki v Kamwanza & 2 others (Civil Case E057 of 2025) [2025] KEMC 44 (KLR), what did the defendants argue regarding the dissolution of the plaintiff's marriage to the deceased and the deceased's living arrangements?
ground_truth: The defendants submitted that the marriage between the plaintiff and the deceased had been dissolved under Kamba customary law, and since the deceased was not married at the time of her death, the court should consider factors such as the deceased's wishes and proximity to her. They contended the deceased lived with the 1st defendant and her children who cared for her during her illness, that the plaintiff never checked on her, was cruel to her, and abandoned her, urging the court to dismiss the plaintiff's claim and enter judgment for their counter-claim.
title: Nzuki v Kamwanza & 2 others (Civil Case E057 of 2025) [2025] KEMC 44 (KLR) (17 March 2025) (Judgment)

question: In defilement cases under the Sexual Offences Act, how can the prosecution prove the age of the victim, and what standard of proof applies?
ground_truth: Age can be proved by medical evidence, a birth certificate, the testimony of the victim's parents or guardian, or by observation and common sense; it is not restricted to documentary or medical evidence. However, since age is a key ingredient of the offence, the prosecution must prove it beyond reasonable doubt, as held in Kaingu Elias Kasono v Republic Criminal Appeal No. 54 of 2010, where the Court of Appeal at Malindi held that age of the victim is a critical component of the charge that must be proved by credible evidence because the sentence upon conviction depends on the age of the victim.
title: Republic v Mgindo (Sexual Offence E008 of 2021) [2025] KEMC 117 (KLR) (14 May 2025) (Judgment)

question: Under section 312 of the Penal Code (Kenya), what constitutes a "false pretence" and what are its essential elements for the offence of obtaining by false pretences?
ground_truth: Section 312 of the Penal Code defines a false pretence as any representation made by words, writing or conduct, of a matter of fact, past or present, which is false and which the maker knows to be false or does not believe to be true. Its elements are: (i) there must be a representation; (ii) it must be by words, writing or conduct; (iii) it must be of a matter of fact; (iv) the fact must be past or present; (v) the representation must be false; and (vi) the person making it must know it to be false or not believe it to be true. Combined with obtaining something capable of being stolen and an intention to defraud, these form the essential elements of the offence of obtaining through false pretences.
title: Republic v Mutua (Criminal Case E068 of 2023) [2025] KEMC 177 (KLR) (31 July 2025) (Ruling)

question: In Republic v Oundo (Criminal Case E028 of 2025) [2025] KEMC 174 (KLR), what did the accused's counsel argue regarding the prosecution's burden to prove compelling reasons for denying bail, citing Republic v Danson Mgunya & another [2010] eKLR and Republic v Dwight Sagaray & others [2013] eKLR?
ground_truth: Counsel submitted that the burden lay on the prosecution to prove the existence of compelling reasons to deny bail (per Republic v Danson Mgunya & another [2010] eKLR), and that to succeed on the ground of witness interference the prosecution must place material before the court demonstrating actual or perceived interference (per Republic v Dwight Sagaray & others [2013] eKLR); it was also argued the accused had secured an alternative place of abode away from the scene.
title: Republic v Oundo (Criminal Case E028 of 2025) [2025] KEMC 174 (KLR) (8 July 2025) (Ruling)

question: In an application for committal to civil jail for failure to pay a decretal sum, what is the determining factor and how did the court define 'inability to pay' in Charles Lutta Kasamani v Concord Insurance Co Ltd & Deputy Registrar Milimani High Court Commercial and Admiralty Division [2018] eKLR?
ground_truth: The court (C. Mwita J.) held that in a committal application, the determining factor is always the judgment debtor's ability to pay; inability to pay means the judgment debtor has completely no means of settling the decree even if given time, and where a decree-holder has obtained a decree from a competent court, that right can be realized through execution, including committal to civil jail as a recognized legal process for enforcement.
title: Nganga v Magambo (Civil Case 1012 of 2021) [2025] KEMC 132 (KLR) (3 June 2025) (Ruling)

question: In Salaries & Remuneration Commission v Gachuiri & 3 others (Civil Appeal E533 & E169 of 2024 (Consolidated)) [2026] KECA 692 (KLR), which bench of Court of Appeal judges heard and determined the consolidated appeal?
ground_truth: The appeal was heard by a bench comprising Justices W. Karanja, P.O. Kiage, K. M'Inoti, W.K. Korir, and G.V. Odunga, sitting at the Court of Appeal at Nairobi.
title: Salaries & Remuneration Commission v Gachuiri & 3 others (Civil Appeal E533 & E169 of 2024 (Consolidated)) [2026] KECA 692 (KLR) (25 March 2026) (Judgment)

question: Under Section 296(2) of the Penal Code, what are the circumstances that constitute the offence of robbery with violence, as set out in Oluoch v Republic (1985) KLR 549?
ground_truth: Robbery with violence is committed if: (a) the offender is armed with a dangerous or offensive weapon or instrument; or (b) the offender is in company with one or more other persons; or (c) at or immediately before or after the robbery, the offender wounds, beats, strikes, or uses other personal violence on any person. Proof of any one of these ingredients is sufficient to sustain a conviction.
title: Republic v Omollo & another (Criminal Case E100 of 2024) [2025] KEMC 127 (KLR) (28 May 2025) (Judgment)

question: In Kenyan law, what did the court state in Republic v Mohamed & Another Petition 39 of 2018 (2019) KESC 47 (KLR) about the purpose of punishing contempt of court?
ground_truth: The court held that an act in contempt of court constitutes an affront to judicial authority and that the court has the liberty and power to mete out a penalty for such conduct in a proper case, the object being firstly to vindicate the court's authority and secondly to safeguard its processes so as to sustain the rule of law and the administration of justice.
title: Ustawi Grain Millers Limited v Hema Bakers Limited; Oliech (Objector); Direct ‘O’ Auctioneers (Interested Party) (Civil Case E727 of 2022) [2025] KEMC 135 (KLR) (3 June 2025) (Ruling)

question: In Registered Trustees Kisii Sports Club v Registered Trustees (Evangelical Lutheran Church of Kenya) (Civil Application E123 of 2025) [2026] KECA 679 (KLR), what did the applicant argue about the test for an arguable appeal in support of its application for extension of time to file a notice of appeal?
ground_truth: The applicant argued that its intended appeal was arguable because it raised weighty issues on ownership, possession, and eviction concerning Kisii municipality block 11/132, and that an arguable appeal need not necessarily succeed—it is enough that it raises at least one bona fide issue deserving the Court's consideration, citing Stanley Kangethe Kinyanjui vs. Tony Ketter & 5 Others [2013] eKLR and Muchugi Kiragu vs. James Muchugi Kiragu & Another Civil Application No. NAI. 356 of 1996.
title: Registered Trustees Kisii Sports Club v Registered Trustees (Evangelical Lutheran Church of Kenya) (Civil Application E123 of 2025) [2026] KECA 679 (KLR) (27 March 2026) (Ruling)

question: Under Rule 63 of the Probate and Administration Rules, does Order 45 of the Civil Procedure Rules (on review) apply to succession proceedings, and what are the grounds for review under Order 45?
ground_truth: Yes. Rule 63 of the Probate and Administration Rules imports certain Civil Procedure Rules, including Order 45, into succession proceedings so far as relevant. Under Order 45, review can only be allowed on the following grounds: (a) discovery of new and important matter of evidence which, after exercise of due diligence, was not within the applicant's knowledge or could not be produced at the time the decree was passed or the order made; (b) mistake or error apparent on the face of the record; or (c) any other sufficient reason which may make the court review its order. This was affirmed in John Mundia Njoroge & 9 others v Cecilia Muthoni Njoroge & another [2016] eKLR, where the court held that Order 45 relating to review is one of the Civil Procedure Rules imported into succession practice by rule 63 of the Probate and Administration Rules.
title: In re Estate of John Njoroge (Deceased) (Succession Cause 738 of 2021) [2025] KEMC 109 (KLR) (20 May 2025) (Ruling)

question: Under the Employment Act, what is the legal distinction between gratuity and severance pay, as discussed in Kigen & 3 others v Sabatia Farmers Co-operative Society Limited?
ground_truth: Gratuity is a payment made by an employer in appreciation of service and has no express provision in the Employment Act; it is usually payable under terms set out in a contract of service or a collective bargaining agreement. Severance pay, by contrast, is only payable under Section 40(g) of the Employment Act where an employee is terminated on account of redundancy.
title: Kigen & 3 others v Sabatia Farmers Co-operative Society Limited (Employment and Labour Relations Cause E059 of 2021) [2025] KEMC 75 (KLR) (29 April 2025) (Judgment)

question: In Republic v National Land Commission & 12 others; M/S Molerise Innovative Services Limited (Ex parte Applicant) (ELC JR Case 4 of 2018), what reasons did the 13th Respondent give for the National Land Commission's cancellation of the Ex-parte Applicant's Letters of Allotment?
ground_truth: The 13th Respondent averred that the Letters of Allotment held by the Ex-parte Applicant were of questionable character due to multiple alterations and inconsistent Survey References, which led to their cancellation by the 1st Respondent (National Land Commission) in its determination pronounced on 15.03.2018.
title: Republic v National Land Commission & 12 others; M/S Molerise Innovative Services Limited (Ex parte Applicant) (Environment and Land Judicial Review Case 4 of 2018) [2026] KEELC 1744 (KLR) (23 March 2026) (Judgment)

question: In Republic v Odaha & another, Criminal Case (Murder) E030 of 2024, which judge delivered the High Court judgment and at which court station, and on what date was it delivered?
ground_truth: The judgment was delivered by Judge DK Kemei at the High Court at Siaya on 24 March 2026.
title: Republic v Odaha & another (Criminal Case (Murder) E030 of 2024) [2026] KEHC 3726 (KLR) (24 March 2026) (Judgment)

question: Under Section 29 of the Children's Act, 2023, who has locus standi to institute court proceedings claiming that a child's rights have been violated, and does a mother qualify?
ground_truth: Section 29(1) allows any person to institute court proceedings claiming that a child's right or fundamental freedom has been denied, violated, infringed or is threatened, and under Sub-Section (2)(a) a parent or guardian can institute such proceedings; thus a mother, as a parent, has locus standi to bring the proceedings.
title: RKP (Suing on behalf of AWS - Minor) v SW (Children's Case E005 of 2024) [2024] KEMC 76 (KLR) (27 November 2024) (Ruling)

question: In the case of Billhouse Investments Limited v Tanui & another (Environment and Land Case E028 of 2025) [2026] KEELC 1723 (KLR), which judge delivered the ruling and at which court station?
ground_truth: The ruling was delivered by Judge GMA Ongondo at the Environment and Land Court at Kapsabet, dated 19 March 2026.
title: Billhouse Investments Limited v Tanui & another (Environment and  Land Case E028 of 2025) [2026] KEELC 1723 (KLR) (19 March 2026) (Ruling)

question: Under Section 74 of the Law of Succession Act, what is the scope of the court's jurisdiction to rectify a grant of representation?
ground_truth: Section 74 limits rectification to correcting errors in names and descriptions, or in setting out the time and place of the deceased's death, or the purpose in a limited grant; the grant of representation, whether before or after confirmation, may be altered and amended accordingly. Such rectification is meant only to correct minor errors that do not substantially interfere with or change the grant and the certificate of grant, not to make substantive changes.
title: In re Estate of Joseph Muchiri Kagwe (Deceased) (Succession Cause 216 of 2016) [2025] KEMC 121 (KLR) (21 March 2025) (Ruling)
